title: Requests for Consular Assistance from Singaporeans in Myanmar Following Military Coup
what_it_is: Requests for Consular Assistance from Singaporeans in Myanmar Following Military Coup

sections.label: Myanmar coup consular assistance questions
sections.summary: Questions ask about consular requests, an ASEAN statement, and impacts after the military detained NLD leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) whether there has been an increase in the number of requests for consular assistance from Singaporeans in Myanmar following the recent military coup; (b) whether ASEAN will be issuing a joint statement on the situation in Myanmar; and (c) how will these developments impact ASEAN and its relations with major powers in the region.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The National League for Democracy (NLD) achieved a landslide victory in the November 2020 General Elections.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In the early hours of 1 February 2021, the military in Myanmar, the Tatmadaw, detained State Counsellor Aung San Suu Kyi, President Win Myint and other leaders of the NLD government.

sections.label: ASEAN external partners dialogue
sections.summary: ASEAN will work with external partners to foster inclusive dialogue and encourage Myanmar's return to democratic transition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: ASEAN will work closely with all its external partners, including the United Nations, the US, China, India, Japan, and the EU, to foster an inclusive dialogue with all key stakeholders and we encourage Myanmar to return to its path of democratic transition.

sections.label: Refugees and Myanmar strategic aspects
sections.summary: ASEAN continues implementing needs assessment recommendations for refugees, and the question asks the Minister's view on strategic developments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: ASEAN will continue the on-going implementation of the Preliminary Needs Assessment's recommendations to improve the plight of these refugees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There are many moving parts for Myanmar – the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration, the ASEAN Charter, a potential collective position of ASEAN on the recent developments and how the military coup will impact the goal of the repatriation of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I want to ask the Minister what are his and MFA's view on the more strategic aspects of the unfolding developments, especially on the goal of a democratic transition in Myanmar.

sections.label: Singapore largest investor in Myanmar
sections.summary: Singapore is Myanmar's largest foreign investor with US$24 billion cumulative approved investments as of December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In fact, Members may be aware that, we, Singapore, is the largest foreign investor in Myanmar and we have cumulative approved investments at US$24 billion, as of December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In fact, this period, the last five years, saw a tenfold increase in Singapore's direct investments in Myanmar compared to the preceding five-year period before that.

sections.label: Reconciliation, release, protest warning
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Win Myint and Aung San Suu Kyi are released for talks, and warns against importing foreign political issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The only way this can happen is if all parties in good faith, sit down, talk, negotiate and achieve reconciliation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And it is in that context that I express my hope that President Win Myint and State Counsellor Aung San Suu Kyi would be released from detention so that they can sit down at the negotiating table and talk.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: One final point: I think Members would be aware that on 5 February, the Singapore Police Force felt compelled to warn against holding protests in relation to the recent developments in Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I want to remind everyone, including foreigners who are visiting, working or residing in Singapore, that they should not import domestic political issues from other countries into Singapore.

sections.label: Peace, engagement, no generalised sanctions
sections.summary: The objective is peace, reconciliation and democratic transition, keeping communication open, and opposing generalised sanctions that hurt ordinary citizens.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Our key objective is to achieve peace, reconciliation, and as I said, to help Myanmar get back on the road of democratic transition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Second, keep lines of communication open and to keep engagement going.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That is why also in that respect, this question of economic sanctions, I think I have explained in my answer just now that we are not in favour of generalised sanctions, which will hurt the ordinary citizens of Myanmar.
